title: HELP - USING THE LIBRARY
entry: Working. Library computer, general reference. Entries are arranged by subject; choose a subject, then an entry, or enter a search term. For operational use, compare any library entry with current sensor readings, duty logs, medical findings, security reports or diplomatic instructions as appropriate. If current verified data conflicts with historical reference material, current data takes precedence. Additional technical, medical or classified detail may require departmental or command authorization. End of entry.

title: VULCAN
entry: Working. Vulcan. Class M homeworld of the Vulcan species and a founding member of the United Federation of Planets, orbiting the star Forty Eridani A. Hot, arid and without a moon, with higher gravity and thinner air than Earth. Visitors are advised to limit exertion until acclimatized. End of entry.

title: SHIKAHR
entry: Working. ShiKahr. A major Vulcan city in the planet's northern desert, an administrative and cultural centre and the site of the current Vulcan-Romulan peace conference. Its architecture favours thick walls, shaded courtyards and water conserved in decorative pools. End of entry.

title: VULCAN SCIENCE ACADEMY
entry: Working. Vulcan Science Academy. Vulcan's foremost institution of research and learning, known throughout the Federation for its standards of evidence and its reluctance to publish a conclusion before it is certain. Commander Spock declined admission in favour of Starfleet, a decision his father did not approve. End of entry.

title: VULCAN HIGH COMMAND
entry: Working. Vulcan High Command. Historical military and governing authority of pre-Federation Vulcan, responsible for the planet's early relations with Earth. Its powers were curtailed during a reform movement of the twenty-second century, and its functions passed to civilian bodies. End of entry.

title: VULCAN COUNCIL
entry: Working. Vulcan Council. The governing council of the planet Vulcan, composed of senior elders and representatives. Council decisions are reached by consensus after extended deliberation. For the current conference, the Council's delegation is led by Councillor T'Seva. End of entry.

title: VULCAN SECURITY
entry: Working. Vulcan Security. The planet's civil security and investigative service. Its officers are trained in observation, interrogation by logic, and the non-lethal restraint of suspects. Federation personnel on Vulcan operate under its jurisdiction unless granted investigative authority. End of entry.

title: SURAK
entry: Working. Surak. Vulcan philosopher, approximately two thousand years before the present, whose teachings ended a period of violent war on Vulcan. Surak taught that emotion must be governed by logic and that violence is the failure of reason. He is regarded as the father of modern Vulcan civilization. End of entry.

title: THE TIME OF AWAKENING
entry: Working. The Time of Awakening. The period in which Surak's teachings spread across Vulcan and the planet abandoned unrestrained emotion for discipline and logic. Those who rejected his teachings left Vulcan. Their descendants are now believed to include the Romulans. End of entry.

title: VULCAN REFORMATION
entry: Working. Vulcan Reformation. General term for the social and religious reforms that followed the Time of Awakening, and for later movements returning Vulcan institutions to Surak's original teachings. End of entry.

title: LOGIC
entry: Working. Logic. To Vulcans, not merely a method of reasoning but a way of life: the disciplined control of emotion so that it does not distort judgment. Logic does not deny that emotions exist. Vulcans experience them intensely, and suppress their expression. End of entry.

title: VULCAN PHILOSOPHY
entry: Working. Vulcan Philosophy. Built on the teachings of Surak: logic, the control of emotion, nonviolence, and the value of diversity. Vulcan schools disagree on interpretation, but rarely on principle, and conduct their disagreements with formal courtesy. End of entry.

title: VULCAN PACIFISM
entry: Working. Vulcan Pacifism. Vulcans hold that killing is wrong and violence a last resort. A Vulcan will defend life when necessary, but will choose the least harmful means available. Vulcan vessels are not armed for aggression. End of entry.

title: KOL-UT-SHAN
entry: Working. Kol-Ut-Shan. Vulcan expression of the principle of Infinite Diversity in Infinite Combinations. See: IDIC. End of entry.

title: IDIC
entry: Working. IDIC. Infinite Diversity in Infinite Combinations. A central Vulcan philosophy holding that the universe is enriched by difference, and that the meeting of differences produces meaning. Represented by a symbol of a circle and a triangle joined by a jewel. End of entry.

title: VULCAN SALUTE
entry: Working. Vulcan Salute. A traditional greeting: the right hand raised, palm forward, the fingers parted between the middle and ring fingers. The customary words are: live long and prosper. The customary reply is: peace and long life. End of entry.

title: VULCAN NERVE PINCH
entry: Working. Vulcan Nerve Pinch. A technique of pressure applied to nerve centres at the base of the neck, causing immediate unconsciousness without lasting injury. It requires precise knowledge of the subject's anatomy. Non-Vulcans who attempt it are rarely successful. End of entry.

title: VULCAN MIND MELD
entry: Working. Vulcan Mind Meld. A telepathic joining of minds by touch, used to share thoughts, memories and experience. The meld is an intimate act, and potentially dangerous to both participants. It is not undertaken lightly, and Vulcan custom discourages its use on the unwilling or the dead. End of entry.

title: VULCAN TELEPATHY
entry: Working. Vulcan Telepathy. Vulcans possess touch telepathy and a limited sensitivity to strong thoughts and emotions at a distance. The ability varies between individuals and is strengthened by training and discipline. End of entry.

title: VULCAN KATRAS
entry: Working. Vulcan Katras. Vulcan belief holds that the living spirit, or katra, may be preserved after death. Outside Vulcan, the practice is little documented and its details are regarded as private. Federation personnel are asked not to question Vulcans on the subject. End of entry.

title: VULCAN HEALING TRANCE
entry: Working. Vulcan Healing Trance. A self-induced trance in which a Vulcan directs the body's resources to healing serious injury. The subject may appear near death. Those attending should not intervene unless instructed; at the proper time, the subject may require vigorous physical stimulation to wake. End of entry.

title: VULCAN PHYSIOLOGY
entry: Working. Vulcan Physiology. Vulcans are humanoid, with pointed ears, upswept eyebrows and greater physical strength than humans. Internal organs differ in position and function: the heart lies where the human liver would be. Normal Vulcan body temperature, pulse and blood pressure would indicate illness in a human. End of entry.

title: VULCAN BLOOD CHEMISTRY
entry: Working. Vulcan Blood Chemistry. Vulcan blood is copper-based and green in colour. Human blood products are incompatible. Medical staff should consult the Vulcan entries of the medical database before any transfusion or drug administration. End of entry.

title: VULCAN HEART
entry: Working. Vulcan Heart. Located in the lower right side of the torso, approximately where the human liver is placed. A normal resting rate is over two hundred beats per minute. Cardiac readings must be interpreted against Vulcan norms. End of entry.

title: VULCAN INNER EYELID
entry: Working. Vulcan Inner Eyelid. A transparent nictitating membrane that protects the eye against the intense light of Vulcan's sun. Its existence was demonstrated aboard this vessel during the Deneva incident. End of entry.

title: VULCAN STRENGTH
entry: Working. Vulcan Strength. Owing to Vulcan's higher gravity, Vulcans are typically several times stronger than humans of similar build. Personnel should bear this in mind in any physical confrontation, and in any friendly one. End of entry.

title: VULCAN LONGEVITY
entry: Working. Vulcan Longevity. Vulcans commonly live to two hundred years or more. Age estimates based on human appearance are unreliable. End of entry.

title: VULCAN DESERT
entry: Working. Vulcan Desert. Much of Vulcan's surface is desert, high, dry and very hot by day. Ruins of the pre-Awakening period remain in remote regions. Travellers should carry water and a communicator, and inform the authorities of their route. End of entry.

title: MOUNT SELEYA
entry: Working. Mount Seleya. A mountain on Vulcan, site of ancient temples and of ceremonies of great significance to Vulcans. Access is restricted. End of entry.

title: VULCAN FORGE
entry: Working. Vulcan Forge. A harsh desert region of Vulcan, associated in Vulcan history with pilgrimages and with the followers of Surak. It is rarely visited by off-worlders. End of entry.

title: VULCAN MARRIAGE
entry: Working. Vulcan Marriage. Vulcans are commonly bonded in childhood by a telepathic link, and the marriage is completed in adulthood in a traditional ceremony. Details are considered private. The Enterprise's records on the subject are brief, and Commander Spock's own are sealed. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN STAR EMPIRE
entry: Working. Romulan Star Empire. Interstellar power beyond the Romulan Neutral Zone, militaristic, expansionist and secretive. No human had seen a Romulan face to face until stardate 1709, during an engagement with this vessel. Romulans are now known to share ancestry with Vulcans. End of entry.

title: ROMULUS
entry: Working. Romulus. Capital world of the Romulan Star Empire. Its location is known; its surface has never been visited by Federation personnel. End of entry.

title: REMUS
entry: Working. Remus. Second world of the Romulan home system, paired in name with Romulus. Earth astronomers named the pair for the twins of Earth's Roman legend. Federation data on its surface and population is negligible. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN SENATE
entry: Working. Romulan Senate. The principal governing body of the Romulan Star Empire, as reported in intercepted communications and the statements of defectors. Its procedures and membership are largely unknown. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN PRAETOR
entry: Working. Romulan Praetor. The title reported for the head of the Romulan state. Federation intelligence has no confirmed identity for the current Praetor. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN MILITARY
entry: Working. Romulan Military. Romulan forces are disciplined, well trained and loyal to the Empire. Romulan commanders have shown themselves capable tacticians who prefer deception, concealment and surprise to open battle. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN INTELLIGENCE
entry: Working. Romulan Intelligence. Romulan agencies conduct espionage, surveillance and covert action beyond the Empire's borders. Their operatives are skilled in infiltration and in the use of false identities. End of entry.

title: TAL SHIAR
entry: Working. Tal Shiar. A name occasionally associated in intercepted traffic with Romulan state intelligence. Federation analysts have not confirmed its meaning, scope or authority. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN NEUTRAL ZONE
entry: Working. Romulan Neutral Zone. A region of space between Federation and Romulan territory, established by treaty in the year twenty-one sixty. Entry by either side without notice is a treaty violation and may be regarded as an act of war. End of entry.

title: EARTH-ROMULAN WAR
entry: Working. Earth-Romulan War. Conflict between Earth and its allies and the Romulan Star Empire in the twenty-second century, fought entirely with primitive atomic weapons and without visual contact between the combatants. It ended with the treaty of twenty-one sixty and the establishment of the Neutral Zone. End of entry.

title: TREATY OF 2160
entry: Working. Treaty of 2160. The treaty ending the Earth-Romulan War, negotiated by subspace radio. It established the Romulan Neutral Zone and the outpost stations that monitor it. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN ISOLATION
entry: Working. Romulan Isolation. For a century after the war, the Romulans made no contact with the Federation. Their re-emergence in twenty-two sixty-six, with a cloaked vessel destroying the Neutral Zone outposts, ended that silence. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN-VULCAN ANCESTRY
entry: Working. Romulan-Vulcan Ancestry. Romulans and Vulcans share a common ancestry. Romulans are believed to be descended from Vulcans who left their homeworld during the Time of Awakening rather than accept the teachings of Surak. Neither people discusses the subject readily. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN PHYSIOLOGY
entry: Working. Romulan Physiology. Romulan physiology is closely similar to Vulcan, including copper-based blood and pointed ears. Romulans do not practice emotional suppression, and their telepathic abilities, if any, are undocumented. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN LANGUAGE
entry: Working. Romulan Language. Romulan is related to ancient Vulcan dialects. The Enterprise's universal translator handles common Romulan speech; technical and military vocabularies may be incomplete. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN RANK STRUCTURE
entry: Working. Romulan Rank Structure. Romulan forces use ranks including Commander, Sub-commander and Centurion. Political officers may accompany military crews. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN COMMANDER
entry: Working. Romulan Commander. A senior Romulan military rank: the commander of a vessel or of a group of vessels. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN CENTURION
entry: Working. Romulan Centurion. A Romulan military rank, typically a senior officer in a ship's crew or an officer commanding troops. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN BIRD-OF-PREY
entry: Working. Romulan Bird-of-Prey. A Romulan warship of the class encountered in twenty-two sixty-six, carrying a plasma energy weapon and a cloaking device, with impulse propulsion only. The hull bears a painted bird on its underside. One vessel of this type is currently impounded at Vulcan. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN D7 BATTLECRUISER
entry: Working. Romulan D7 Battlecruiser. Romulan forces have been observed operating vessels of Klingon D7 design, indicating an exchange of technology between the two powers. Romulan D7s are equipped with cloaking devices. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN PLASMA WEAPON
entry: Working. Romulan Plasma Weapon. A short-range energy weapon of enormous destructive power, fired as a bolt of plasma. Its strength diminishes with distance; at extreme range, it may be outrun. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN CLOAKING DEVICE
entry: Working. Romulan Cloaking Device. A device that renders a vessel invisible to sight and to most sensors. A cloaked vessel cannot fire its weapons, and uses significant power. A working device was obtained by this vessel in twenty-two sixty-eight, under orders. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN DISRUPTOR
entry: Working. Romulan Disruptor. A Romulan hand weapon and ship's weapon firing a beam of disruptive energy, comparable to a phaser on the killing setting. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN WARBIRD TERMINOLOGY
entry: Working. Romulan Warbird Terminology. Starfleet personnel commonly refer to Romulan warships as warbirds. The term is informal and does not refer to a specific class. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN ESPIONAGE
entry: Working. Romulan Espionage. Romulan intelligence has penetrated Federation communications and installations in the past. Personnel should report any unusual contact, request or equipment fault that could indicate Romulan interest. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN INFILTRATION
entry: Working. Romulan Infiltration. Owing to their Vulcan appearance, Romulan agents can pass as Vulcans to all but close medical or telepathic examination. Identity verification on Vulcan should not rely on appearance. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN DEFECTION
entry: Working. Romulan Defection. Romulans who leave the Empire are rare and are regarded at home as traitors. Defectors may hold valuable information; they may also be agents. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN HONOR
entry: Working. Romulan Honor. Romulans place great value on personal and military honour, and on duty to the Empire. A Romulan commander may choose death over capture or disgrace. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN POLITICS
entry: Working. Romulan Politics. Romulan politics are believed to involve intense competition between factions, families and military commands. Policy toward the Federation may change with the faction in power. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN-FEDERATION RELATIONS
entry: Working. Romulan-Federation Relations. Relations are hostile but governed by treaty. The Neutral Zone is respected by both sides, with exceptions. The current Vulcan-Romulan peace initiative is the first official contact in many years. End of entry.

title: UNITED FEDERATION OF PLANETS
entry: Working. United Federation of Planets. An interstellar union of member worlds, founded in twenty-one sixty-one by Earth, Vulcan, Andoria, Tellar and others, committed to peaceful cooperation, exploration and mutual defence. End of entry.

title: FEDERATION COUNCIL
entry: Working. Federation Council. The legislative body of the Federation, composed of representatives of the member worlds. It meets on Earth, at Paris. End of entry.

title: FEDERATION PRESIDENT
entry: Working. Federation President. The chief executive of the United Federation of Planets, elected by the Council. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET
entry: Working. Starfleet. The deep-space exploratory and defence service of the United Federation of Planets. Its mission is exploration, scientific research, diplomacy and the defence of the Federation. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET COMMAND
entry: Working. Starfleet Command. The headquarters and senior authority of Starfleet, located in San Francisco, Earth. Starship commanders report to Starfleet Command, though distances often require them to act on their own judgment. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET ACADEMY
entry: Working. Starfleet Academy. Starfleet's officer training institution, in San Francisco. The course is four years. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET GENERAL ORDERS
entry: Working. Starfleet General Orders. Standing orders that apply to all Starfleet personnel and vessels. They take precedence over local orders except where the commanding officer judges that circumstances require otherwise, and is prepared to justify the decision. End of entry.

title: PRIME DIRECTIVE
entry: Working. Prime Directive. Starfleet General Order One. No Starfleet personnel may interfere with the normal development of any society, and a starship commander may sacrifice his vessel and crew rather than violate it. End of entry.

title: GENERAL ORDER SEVEN
entry: Working. General Order Seven. No vessel under any condition, emergency or otherwise, is to visit Talos Four. Violation is the only death penalty remaining on Federation record. End of entry.

title: GENERAL ORDER TWENTY-FOUR
entry: Working. General Order Twenty-Four. An order, given by a starship commander, to destroy a planet's surface within a set period. It requires confirmation and may be countermanded by the commander. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET REGULATIONS
entry: Working. Starfleet Regulations. The body of rules governing Starfleet conduct, procedure and discipline. Regulation numbers are cited in log entries and reports; a copy is available on request at any library station. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET CHAIN OF COMMAND
entry: Working. Starfleet Chain of Command. Authority passes from the commanding officer to the first officer, then to the senior officers in order of rank. In the commanding officer's absence, the senior officer aboard assumes command. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET RANK STRUCTURE
entry: Working. Starfleet Rank Structure. Officer ranks include ensign, lieutenant junior grade, lieutenant, lieutenant commander, commander, captain and commodore, with admirals above. Rank is shown by gold braid on the sleeves. End of entry.

title: COMMAND DIVISION
entry: Working. Command Division. Starfleet personnel in command, navigation and helm duties. Uniform colour: gold. End of entry.

title: SCIENCES DIVISION
entry: Working. Sciences Division. Starfleet personnel in the sciences and medicine. Uniform colour: blue. End of entry.

title: OPERATIONS DIVISION
entry: Working. Operations Division. Starfleet personnel in engineering, communications, security and support services. Uniform colour: red. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET MEDICAL
entry: Working. Starfleet Medical. Starfleet's medical service, responsible for the health of personnel and for medical research. The ship's chief medical officer may relieve any officer, including the captain, on medical grounds. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET SECURITY
entry: Working. Starfleet Security. Shipboard and station security personnel, responsible for the protection of the vessel, its crew and its passengers. Aboard the Enterprise, security is commanded by Lieutenant Commander Giotto. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET ENGINEERING
entry: Working. Starfleet Engineering. Responsible for the design, operation and maintenance of starships and their systems. Aboard the Enterprise, engineering is commanded by Lieutenant Commander Montgomery Scott. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET INTELLIGENCE
entry: Working. Starfleet Intelligence. The intelligence service of Starfleet. Its operations are classified. Enterprise personnel have, on occasion, carried out missions on its behalf. End of entry.

title: FEDERATION DIPLOMATIC CORPS
entry: Working. Federation Diplomatic Corps. The Federation's body of ambassadors and diplomatic staff. Starships frequently carry diplomatic personnel and may be assigned to protect conferences. End of entry.

title: AMBASSADORIAL IMMUNITY
entry: Working. Ambassadorial Immunity. Accredited diplomats are protected from arrest and prosecution under the law of the host world. Immunity may be waived by the diplomat's own government. Suspicion alone does not remove it. End of entry.

title: DIPLOMATIC CONFERENCE
entry: Working. Diplomatic Conference. A formal meeting of delegations to negotiate an agreement. Security, protocol and the confidentiality of proceedings are the responsibility of the host world, assisted where requested by Starfleet. End of entry.

title: PEACE CONFERENCE
entry: Working. Peace Conference. A diplomatic conference held to end or prevent hostilities. Its success often depends as much on trust as on terms. End of entry.

title: CEASEFIRE
entry: Working. Ceasefire. An agreed suspension of hostilities. It does not end a conflict, and may be broken by either side. End of entry.

title: ARMISTICE
entry: Working. Armistice. A formal agreement to end active hostilities, pending a final treaty. End of entry.

title: TREATY
entry: Working. Treaty. A formal agreement between governments. Federation treaties require ratification by the Federation Council. End of entry.

title: DIPLOMATIC CREDENTIALS
entry: Working. Diplomatic Credentials. Documents establishing a diplomat's identity and authority to act for a government. On Vulcan, credentials are recorded and verified by the conference secretariat. Forged credentials are a serious offence. End of entry.

title: SHORE LEAVE
entry: Working. Shore Leave. Authorised leave from duty, taken on a planet or station. Personnel on shore leave remain subject to Starfleet regulations and may be recalled at any time. End of entry.

title: COURT MARTIAL
entry: Working. Court Martial. A Starfleet military court convened to try serious charges against personnel. The accused is entitled to counsel and to a hearing before a board of officers. End of entry.

title: USS ENTERPRISE NCC-1701
entry: Working. U.S.S. Enterprise, N C C one seven zero one. A Constitution class heavy cruiser of Starfleet, launched from the San Francisco Yards and commanded by Captain James T. Kirk on a five-year mission of exploration. Complement: four hundred and thirty. End of entry.

title: CONSTITUTION CLASS
entry: Working. Constitution Class. Starfleet's premier class of heavy cruiser, capable of extended deep-space operation without support. A primary hull, a secondary hull and two warp nacelles. Length two hundred and eighty-nine metres. End of entry.

title: PRIMARY HULL
entry: Working. Primary Hull. The saucer-shaped forward section of a Constitution class starship, containing the bridge, crew quarters, sickbay and most of the ship's living and working space. Decks are numbered downward from the bridge, Deck One. End of entry.

title: SECONDARY HULL
entry: Working. Secondary Hull. The engineering hull below and behind the saucer, containing main engineering, the shuttlecraft hangar and cargo spaces. It supports the warp nacelles. End of entry.

title: BRIDGE
entry: Working. Bridge. Command centre of the ship, on Deck One at the top of the primary hull. Stations ring the captain's chair: helm and navigation forward, with communications, science, engineering, weapons and environmental stations around the outer wall. End of entry.

title: MAIN VIEWSCREEN
entry: Working. Main Viewscreen. The large screen at the forward end of the bridge, showing external views, magnified images and incoming visual communications. End of entry.

title: CAPTAIN'S CHAIR
entry: Working. Captain's Chair. The command position at the centre of the bridge, with controls for intercom, alert status and recording the captain's log. End of entry.

title: HELM STATION
entry: Working. Helm Station. The forward console at which the helmsman controls the ship's speed, heading and weapons. Aboard the Enterprise, normally Lieutenant Sulu. End of entry.

title: NAVIGATION STATION
entry: Working. Navigation Station. The forward console beside the helm, responsible for course plotting, position and astrogation. Aboard the Enterprise, normally Ensign Chekov. End of entry.

title: COMMUNICATIONS STATION
entry: Working. Communications Station. The bridge station responsible for ship-to-ship, ship-to-surface and internal communications, and for the monitoring of subspace traffic. Aboard the Enterprise, normally Lieutenant Uhura. End of entry.

title: SCIENCE STATION
entry: Working. Science Station. The bridge station that controls the ship's sensors and the library computer. Aboard the Enterprise, normally Commander Spock, science officer. End of entry.

title: ENGINEERING STATION
entry: Working. Engineering Station. The bridge station that monitors the engines, power and ship's systems, and relays orders to main engineering. End of entry.

title: MAIN ENGINEERING
entry: Working. Main Engineering. The ship's engineering control room, on Deck Seven, from which the warp and impulse engines and the ship's power are controlled. Under the command of the chief engineer. End of entry.

title: AUXILIARY CONTROL
entry: Working. Auxiliary Control. A secondary control room, on Deck Fifteen, from which the ship can be navigated and operated if the bridge is lost. Its systems can override bridge control. Access is restricted. End of entry.

title: SICKBAY
entry: Working. Sickbay. The ship's hospital, on Deck Seven, with examination rooms, diagnostic beds, a laboratory and an intensive care ward. Under the command of the chief medical officer, Doctor McCoy. End of entry.

title: TRANSPORTER ROOM
entry: Working. Transporter Room. A compartment containing a transporter platform and its control console. The Enterprise's principal personnel transporters are on Deck Seven. Transporter Room One is under the charge of Lieutenant Kyle. End of entry.

title: SHUTTLECRAFT HANGAR
entry: Working. Shuttlecraft Hangar. The hangar deck at the rear of the secondary hull, from which shuttlecraft are launched and recovered through the clamshell bay doors. The hangar must be depressurised before the doors are opened. End of entry.

title: BRIG
entry: Working. Brig. The ship's detention cells, secured by force fields, under the control of the security department. End of entry.

title: SECURITY OFFICE
entry: Working. Security Office. The headquarters of the ship's security department on Deck Seven, including the evidence locker and the duty roster. End of entry.

title: ARMORY
entry: Working. Armory. A secured compartment where hand phasers and other weapons are stored and maintained. Issue requires authorization. End of entry.

title: BRIEFING ROOM
entry: Working. Briefing Room. A meeting room equipped with a table viewscreen and computer access, used for officers' conferences and mission briefings. End of entry.

title: CAPTAIN'S QUARTERS
entry: Working. Captain's Quarters. The commanding officer's private cabin. Entry without the captain's permission is not customary, by long tradition and the chief engineer's firm opinion. End of entry.

title: CREW QUARTERS
entry: Working. Crew Quarters. Living accommodation for the ship's company. Officers occupy single cabins; junior crew share. Each cabin has a bed, a desk, a computer terminal, a food slot and a washroom. End of entry.

title: RECREATION DECK
entry: Working. Recreation Deck. Areas set aside for recreation, exercise and social activity, essential to the crew's wellbeing on a long mission. End of entry.

title: GYMNASIUM
entry: Working. Gymnasium. A facility for physical training, including fencing, wrestling and martial arts. End of entry.

title: BOWLING ALLEY
entry: Working. Bowling Alley. A recreation facility of several lanes, with an automatic scoring system. Competition between departments is keen. End of entry.

title: JEFFERIES TUBE
entry: Working. Jefferies Tube. A crawlway giving access to the ship's circuitry and conduits. Named for an early starship engineer. Tubes are identified by deck and letter, for example Six-A. End of entry.

title: TURBOLIFT
entry: Working. Turbolift. The ship's internal transport, moving horizontally and vertically through the hull. Controlled by voice command or by the handles in each car. End of entry.

title: OBSERVATION LOUNGE
entry: Working. Observation Lounge. A lounge with a large viewport, available to off-duty personnel. The Deck Five officers' lounge is a frequent meeting place. End of entry.

title: EMERGENCY MANUAL MONITOR
entry: Working. Emergency Manual Monitor. A control position from which ship functions may be monitored and directed by hand during an emergency or computer failure. End of entry.

title: WARP DRIVE
entry: Working. Warp Drive. The faster-than-light propulsion system of Federation starships. Warp coils in the nacelles generate a field that allows the ship to travel faster than light without violating physical law within the field. End of entry.

title: WARP FACTOR
entry: Working. Warp Factor. The measure of a vessel's speed above the speed of light. Speed increases with the cube of the warp factor: warp two is eight times the speed of light. The Enterprise's maximum safe speed is warp six; warp eight is possible for brief periods at great risk. End of entry.

title: WARP FIELD
entry: Working. Warp Field. The field of energy generated by the warp nacelles that surrounds the ship at warp. Instability in the field may damage the ship or its crew. End of entry.

title: WARP NACELLE
entry: Working. Warp Nacelle. One of the two long engine pods mounted above and behind the secondary hull, containing the warp coils. The forward end of each nacelle carries a glowing collector assembly. End of entry.

title: MATTER-ANTIMATTER REACTION
entry: Working. Matter-Antimatter Reaction. The ship's principal power source. Matter and antimatter annihilate one another, controlled and focused through dilithium crystals, to release the energy that drives the warp engines. End of entry.

title: ANTIMATTER
entry: Working. Antimatter. Matter of reversed charge, which annihilates on contact with normal matter. It is contained in magnetic fields. Any failure of containment would destroy the ship. End of entry.

title: DEUTERIUM
entry: Working. Deuterium. Heavy hydrogen, used as fuel by the ship's engines. End of entry.

title: DILITHIUM
entry: Working. Dilithium. A rare crystalline mineral that regulates the matter-antimatter reaction. Dilithium is essential to warp drive and is a strategic resource; the Federation, the Klingons and the Romulans all seek it. End of entry.

title: DILITHIUM CRYSTAL CONVERTER
entry: Working. Dilithium Crystal Converter. The assembly in which dilithium crystals focus and regulate the matter-antimatter reaction. Crystals degrade with use and must be replaced or realigned. End of entry.

title: MAIN ENERGIZER
entry: Working. Main Energizer. The system that distributes power from the engines to the ship's systems. End of entry.

title: IMPULSE DRIVE
entry: Working. Impulse Drive. The ship's sublight propulsion, used for manoeuvring and travel within star systems. End of entry.

title: IMPULSE ENGINE
entry: Working. Impulse Engine. The engine assembly at the rear of the primary hull that provides sublight thrust. The impulse engines can provide power for essential systems if the warp engines fail. End of entry.

title: REACTION CONTROL THRUSTER
entry: Working. Reaction Control Thruster. Small manoeuvring thrusters on the hull, used for fine control of attitude and position. End of entry.

title: EMERGENCY POWER
entry: Working. Emergency Power. Power from emergency systems, used to maintain life support, lighting and communications when main power fails. End of entry.

title: AUXILIARY POWER
entry: Working. Auxiliary Power. Secondary power sources that supplement or replace main power. End of entry.

title: RESERVE POWER
entry: Working. Reserve Power. Power held in batteries for use when main and auxiliary power are unavailable. Its duration is limited. End of entry.

title: POWER DISTRIBUTION
entry: Working. Power Distribution. The network of conduits and junctions carrying power from the engines to the ship's systems. Power can be rerouted in an emergency. End of entry.

title: EPS EQUIVALENT SYSTEMS
entry: Working. E P S Equivalent Systems. The ship's power transfer conduits and junctions. See: Power Distribution. End of entry.

title: ENGINEERING CONTROL
entry: Working. Engineering Control. The panels in main engineering from which the engines are controlled and their output monitored. End of entry.

title: COLD RESTART
entry: Working. Cold Restart. Restarting the warp engines from a complete shutdown, with no warp energy in the system. The procedure takes approximately thirty minutes and cannot be hurried. End of entry.

title: WARP CORE SHUTDOWN
entry: Working. Warp Core Shutdown. A controlled shutdown of the warp engines, necessary for maintenance or when the reaction becomes unstable. A ship in shutdown has impulse power only. End of entry.

title: ENGINE OVERLOAD
entry: Working. Engine Overload. A dangerous condition in which the matter-antimatter reaction exceeds safe limits. Unchecked, it ends in the destruction of the ship. End of entry.

title: STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY
entry: Working. Structural Integrity. The strength of the ship's hull and frame, reinforced by an integrity field. At high warp, structural integrity is the principal limit on speed. End of entry.

title: INERTIAL DAMPENING
entry: Working. Inertial Dampening. A system that protects the crew from the forces of acceleration. Without it, any significant manoeuvre would be fatal. End of entry.

title: ARTIFICIAL GRAVITY
entry: Working. Artificial Gravity. Gravity generated by plating in the decks, maintained at Earth normal. End of entry.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROL
entry: Working. Environmental Control. The systems that regulate air, temperature, pressure and humidity throughout the ship. End of entry.

title: LIFE SUPPORT
entry: Working. Life Support. The systems that sustain the crew: air, water, temperature and gravity. Life support is given priority over every other system in a power emergency. End of entry.

title: DAMAGE CONTROL
entry: Working. Damage Control. The organisation and procedures for containing and repairing damage. Damage control parties report to the first officer and the chief engineer. End of entry.

title: EMERGENCY BULKHEAD
entry: Working. Emergency Bulkhead. A bulkhead that seals automatically to isolate a damaged section of the ship. End of entry.

title: PRESSURE DOOR
entry: Working. Pressure Door. A door designed to hold atmospheric pressure, closing automatically when a loss of pressure is detected. End of entry.

title: HULL BREACH
entry: Working. Hull Breach. A rupture of the hull, causing loss of atmosphere. Emergency bulkheads seal the affected section. End of entry.

title: TRANSPORTER
entry: Working. Transporter. A device that converts matter into an energy pattern, transmits it to a destination, and reassembles it. Range approximately sixteen thousand miles. Shields must be lowered to transport. End of entry.

title: TRANSPORTER BEAM
entry: Working. Transporter Beam. The beam of energy that carries a pattern between the transporter and its destination. End of entry.

title: TRANSPORTER PAD
entry: Working. Transporter Pad. One of the six positions on the transporter platform, each able to transport one person. End of entry.

title: TRANSPORTER CONSOLE
entry: Working. Transporter Console. The control station from which the operator sets coordinates, locks on and energises. End of entry.

title: TRANSPORTER COORDINATES
entry: Working. Transporter Coordinates. The location, in three dimensions, to which a pattern is to be sent or from which it is to be retrieved. Errors in coordinates may materialise a subject inside solid matter. End of entry.

title: PATTERN BUFFER
entry: Working. Pattern Buffer. The part of the transporter in which a subject's pattern is held during transport. A pattern may be held there briefly. Long storage is not recommended. End of entry.

title: ANNULAR CONFINEMENT BEAM
entry: Working. Annular Confinement Beam. A component of the transporter beam that holds the subject's pattern together during transport. End of entry.

title: MOLECULAR IMAGING SCANNER
entry: Working. Molecular Imaging Scanner. The transporter scanners that record a subject's structure before dematerialisation. End of entry.

title: HEISENBERG COMPENSATOR
entry: Working. Heisenberg Compensator. A transporter component that allows the subject to be accurately reassembled despite the limits of measurement. Its operating principle is classified. End of entry.

title: TRANSPORTER LOCK
entry: Working. Transporter Lock. The fixing of the transporter on a subject. A lock may be prevented by interference, shielding, or the absence of a communicator signal. End of entry.

title: TRANSPORTER TRACE
entry: Working. Transporter Trace. A record of a transport's origin and destination, stored in the transporter log. End of entry.

title: TRANSPORTER LOG
entry: Working. Transporter Log. The record of every transport made, with time, coordinates and operator. Entries may only be deleted by authorised personnel. End of entry.

title: TRANSPORTER MALFUNCTION
entry: Working. Transporter Malfunction. A failure of the transporter during operation. Malfunctions have produced duplicates, transfers to a parallel universe, and the loss of personnel. All transporter faults must be reported. End of entry.

title: TRANSPORTER INTERFERENCE
entry: Working. Transporter Interference. Ion storms, magnetic fields, certain minerals and deflector shields all interfere with transport. End of entry.

title: EMERGENCY BEAM-OUT
entry: Working. Emergency Beam-out. The immediate recovery of personnel from danger, on locking coordinates without waiting for a request. End of entry.

title: SITE-TO-SITE TRANSPORT
entry: Working. Site-to-site Transport. Transport between two locations without materialising on the ship's platform. Its use is restricted to emergencies. End of entry.

title: CARGO TRANSPORTER
entry: Working. Cargo Transporter. A transporter designed for cargo rather than personnel, with a larger platform. Cargo transporters can transport people if adjusted, with greater risk. End of entry.

title: SHUTTLECRAFT
entry: Working. Shuttlecraft. A small auxiliary craft for travel between the ship and a planet, or between ships, at sublight or low warp speeds. End of entry.

title: CLASS F SHUTTLECRAFT
entry: Working. Class F Shuttlecraft. The standard Starfleet shuttlecraft, with a crew of two and seating for several passengers. End of entry.

title: GALILEO
entry: Working. Galileo. The Enterprise shuttlecraft lost at Taurus Two in twenty-two sixty-seven, with two of its crew. A replacement now carries the name. End of entry.

title: SHUTTLECRAFT NAVIGATION
entry: Working. Shuttlecraft Navigation. Shuttlecraft navigation uses its own sensors and a link to the parent vessel. Its range is limited. End of entry.

title: SHUTTLECRAFT HANGAR OPERATIONS
entry: Working. Shuttlecraft Hangar Operations. Launch requires the hangar deck to be cleared and depressurised and the bay doors opened under control of the hangar deck officer. End of entry.

title: DOCKING PROCEDURE
entry: Working. Docking Procedure. The procedure for docking a shuttlecraft or vessel at a station or ship, controlled by tractor beam or by hand. End of entry.

title: LANDING PARTY
entry: Working. Landing Party. Personnel sent to a planet's surface. Landing parties carry communicators, and phasers and tricorders as required, and must report at set intervals. End of entry.

title: BEAM-DOWN PROCEDURE
entry: Working. Beam-down Procedure. Personnel take position on the platform; the operator locks on to the coordinates and energises on the command of the senior officer. End of entry.

title: BEAM-UP PROCEDURE
entry: Working. Beam-up Procedure. On a request by communicator, the transporter locks on to the communicator signal and recovers the party. End of entry.

title: ORBITAL INSERTION
entry: Working. Orbital Insertion. The manoeuvre by which a ship enters orbit about a planet. End of entry.

title: STANDARD ORBIT
entry: Working. Standard Orbit. The standard parking orbit about a planet, from which transporter and sensors may operate. End of entry.

title: GEOSYNCHRONOUS ORBIT
entry: Working. Geosynchronous Orbit. An orbit in which the ship remains above the same point on a planet's surface. End of entry.

title: ESCAPE VELOCITY
entry: Working. Escape Velocity. The speed a vessel must reach to leave a planet's gravity without further thrust. Starships in orbit are already moving at orbital velocity; leaving orbit requires much less. End of entry.

title: ENTERPRISE COMPUTER
entry: Working. Enterprise Computer. The ship's central computer, which controls or monitors nearly every system aboard and holds the library. It answers spoken questions and commands from authorised personnel. End of entry.

title: DUOTRONIC COMPUTER
entry: Working. Duotronic Computer. The computer technology in use aboard Starfleet vessels, developed by Doctor Richard Daystrom. The Enterprise's computer is a duotronic system. End of entry.

title: COMPUTER CORE
entry: Working. Computer Core. The ship's central computer installation, housing its processors and memory banks. The Enterprise's computer core is reached from Deck Seven. End of entry.

title: MEMORY BANK
entry: Working. Memory Bank. A unit of the computer's memory storage. Damage to a memory bank may lose or corrupt the records it holds. End of entry.

title: COMPUTER ACCESS CODE
entry: Working. Computer Access Code. A code that identifies a user to the computer and determines what that user may see and change. End of entry.

title: COMMAND AUTHORIZATION
entry: Working. Command Authorization. The authority to issue orders to the computer at command level, held by the captain and senior officers and confirmed by voice print and code. End of entry.

title: SECURITY LOCKOUT
entry: Working. Security Lockout. A condition in which the computer refuses commands from all but a specified authority, used to protect critical systems. End of entry.

title: COMPUTER OVERRIDE
entry: Working. Computer Override. A command that takes control of a system away from its normal operator. Override commands are logged. End of entry.

title: COMPUTER VIRUS
entry: Working. Computer Virus. A program designed to spread through a computer's systems and alter or damage them. The computer's defences are designed to detect such programs; a sufficiently advanced one may conceal itself. End of entry.

title: COMPUTER SABOTAGE
entry: Working. Computer Sabotage. Deliberate interference with the computer or its records. Suspected sabotage should be reported to the captain and the chief engineer, and the affected system isolated. End of entry.

title: CORRUPTED MEMORY
entry: Working. Corrupted Memory. Computer records that have been damaged or altered so that they can no longer be trusted. The computer may report corrupted memory as missing, or not at all. End of entry.

title: DELETED COMPUTER RECORD
entry: Working. Deleted Computer Record. A record removed from active memory. Deleted records may survive in backup storage, in system logs, or in the memory of other systems that received them. End of entry.

title: SENSOR ARRAY
entry: Working. Sensor Array. The ship's sensors: instruments that detect and measure objects, energy and life at a distance. Sensor data is analysed by the computer and displayed at the science station. End of entry.

title: LONG-RANGE SENSORS
entry: Working. Long-range Sensors. Sensors able to detect objects at great distances, with reduced detail. End of entry.

title: SHORT-RANGE SENSORS
entry: Working. Short-range Sensors. Sensors used at close range for detailed scans of vessels, planets and life forms. End of entry.

title: INTERNAL SENSORS
entry: Working. Internal Sensors. Sensors throughout the ship that monitor its systems and detect the life forms aboard. Internal sensors can be deceived or blocked. End of entry.

title: LIFE-FORM SCAN
entry: Working. Life-form Scan. A sensor scan that detects and identifies living beings by their life signs. End of entry.

title: BIO-SENSOR
entry: Working. Bio-sensor. A sensor that detects biological activity or monitors the vital signs of a patient. End of entry.

title: TRICORDER
entry: Working. Tricorder. A portable sensor, computer and recording device used by landing parties and technicians. It records what it detects, and its recordings can be played back or transferred to the ship's computer. End of entry.

title: MEDICAL TRICORDER
entry: Working. Medical Tricorder. A tricorder fitted with a medical scanner for diagnosing patients in the field. End of entry.

title: SCIENCE TRICORDER
entry: Working. Science Tricorder. A tricorder configured for scientific and technical investigation. End of entry.

title: SUBSPACE RADIO
entry: Working. Subspace Radio. Communication through subspace, faster than light, between ships, stations and planets. Over very long distances, messages may take days or weeks to arrive. End of entry.

title: SUBSPACE COMMUNICATION
entry: Working. Subspace Communication. See: Subspace Radio. Subspace transmissions may be jammed, intercepted or disrupted by natural phenomena. End of entry.

title: SHIP-TO-SHIP COMMUNICATION
entry: Working. Ship-to-ship Communication. Communication between vessels by radio or subspace, by voice or visual channel. End of entry.

title: COMMUNICATOR
entry: Working. Communicator. The hand communicator carried by Starfleet personnel for communication with the ship and with one another. It also provides the transporter with a lock signal. End of entry.

title: UNIVERSAL TRANSLATOR
entry: Working. Universal Translator. A device that analyses an unfamiliar language and translates it. It is built into the ship's communications systems. End of entry.

title: ENCRYPTION
entry: Working. Encryption. The coding of communications or records so that only those with the key can read them. End of entry.

title: DECRYPTION
entry: Working. Decryption. The decoding of encrypted communications or records. Complex encryption may take the computer hours or days to break. End of entry.

title: SIGNAL TRACE
entry: Working. Signal Trace. The tracing of a transmission back to its source. End of entry.

title: SENSOR GHOST
entry: Working. Sensor Ghost. A false or unexplained sensor reading. Ghosts may be caused by equipment fault, natural phenomena or deliberate deception. End of entry.

title: TELEMETRY
entry: Working. Telemetry. Data transmitted automatically from a ship's systems, a probe or a shuttlecraft to a monitoring station. End of entry.

title: PHASER
entry: Working. Phaser. The standard energy weapon of Starfleet, available as a hand weapon and as a ship's weapon. Settings range from stun to heat and disintegration. End of entry.

title: PHASER TYPE ONE
entry: Working. Phaser Type One. A small hand phaser, easily concealed, carried by landing parties. End of entry.

title: PHASER TYPE TWO
entry: Working. Phaser Type Two. A larger pistol phaser, into which the type one fits. More powerful and with a longer charge. End of entry.

title: SHIP'S PHASERS
entry: Working. Ship's Phasers. The Enterprise's main energy weapons, mounted on the primary hull. End of entry.

title: PHASER STUN SETTING
entry: Working. Phaser Stun Setting. A setting that renders the target unconscious without lasting harm. Effects vary between species. End of entry.

title: PHASER KILL SETTING
entry: Working. Phaser Kill Setting. A setting that kills or disintegrates the target. Its use requires justification. End of entry.

title: PHASER OVERLOAD
entry: Working. Phaser Overload. A phaser set to overload builds to an explosion after a short period, signalled by a rising whine. It is used as a demolition charge. End of entry.

title: PHOTON TORPEDO
entry: Working. Photon Torpedo. A ship's weapon carrying a charge of matter and antimatter, fired from torpedo tubes. End of entry.

title: PHOTON TORPEDO TUBE
entry: Working. Photon Torpedo Tube. The launcher from which photon torpedoes are fired. End of entry.

title: DEFLECTOR SHIELD
entry: Working. Deflector Shield. A field of energy that protects the ship from attack and collision. While the shields are up, the transporter cannot be used. End of entry.

title: DEFLECTOR SCREEN
entry: Working. Deflector Screen. See: Deflector Shield. End of entry.

title: NAVIGATIONAL DEFLECTOR
entry: Working. Navigational Deflector. The deflector that sweeps space dust and debris from the ship's path at speed. End of entry.

title: COMBAT ALERT
entry: Working. Combat Alert. A state of readiness for combat. End of entry.

title: RED ALERT
entry: Working. Red Alert. The highest state of alert. All personnel to battle stations; shields and weapons ready. Announced by klaxon and by red alert indicators throughout the ship. End of entry.

title: YELLOW ALERT
entry: Working. Yellow Alert. A state of heightened readiness, short of red alert. End of entry.

title: SECURITY ALERT
entry: Working. Security Alert. An alert for a security threat aboard ship, summoning security personnel. End of entry.

title: INTRUDER ALERT
entry: Working. Intruder Alert. An alert announcing an intruder aboard ship. Security teams search the ship, and turbolift and door access may be restricted. End of entry.

title: BOARDING PARTY
entry: Working. Boarding Party. Personnel who board another vessel, or hostile personnel who board this one. End of entry.

title: INTERNAL SECURITY
entry: Working. Internal Security. The protection of the ship from threats aboard: intruders, sabotage, and crime. End of entry.

title: SECURITY TEAM
entry: Working. Security Team. A group of security personnel assigned to a task. Security teams carry phasers on stun unless ordered otherwise. End of entry.

title: BRIG PROCEDURE
entry: Working. Brig Procedure. Prisoners are searched, their property recorded and secured, and placed in a cell behind a force field. A guard is posted. End of entry.

title: EVIDENCE LOCKER
entry: Working. Evidence Locker. A secured locker in the security office in which evidence is held under record. Items are released only on a signed requisition. End of entry.

title: FORCE FIELD
entry: Working. Force Field. A barrier of energy used to confine prisoners, protect areas or contain hazards. Force fields can be lowered by authorised personnel, or overloaded. End of entry.

title: CONTAINMENT FIELD
entry: Working. Containment Field. A force field used to contain a hazardous substance or object. End of entry.

title: FIELD ISOLATOR
entry: Working. Field Isolator. A device for isolating one strand of a force field, power line or circuit from the rest, so that it can be cut or bypassed without alerting the system. A Romulan instrument of this kind is held in the Enterprise's evidence locker. End of entry.

title: PERSONAL RESTRAINT
entry: Working. Personal Restraint. A device for restraining a prisoner. Restraints are used only when necessary. End of entry.

title: SHIPBOARD SABOTAGE
entry: Working. Shipboard Sabotage. Deliberate damage to a ship's systems from within. See: Computer Sabotage. End of entry.

title: UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS
entry: Working. Unauthorized Access. Entry to a restricted area or system without authority. All unauthorised access is logged and reported. End of entry.

title: MUTINY
entry: Working. Mutiny. The seizure of command of a vessel from its lawful commander. Mutiny is a capital offence under Starfleet regulations. End of entry.

title: HIJACKING
entry: Working. Hijacking. The seizure of a vessel by force or deception. End of entry.

title: SELF-DESTRUCT
entry: Working. Self-destruct. A sequence that destroys the ship to prevent its capture. It requires the authorisation codes of the captain and two senior officers, and can be cancelled before the end of the countdown. End of entry.

title: STARFLEET MEDICAL DATABASE
entry: Working. Starfleet Medical Database. The medical records and reference library available to the ship's medical staff, including the physiology of known species. End of entry.

title: SICKBAY PROCEDURE
entry: Working. Sickbay Procedure. Patients are admitted, examined and treated under the authority of the chief medical officer. Visitors are admitted at the doctor's discretion. End of entry.

title: BIOBED
entry: Working. Biobed. A sickbay bed fitted with sensors that monitor the patient's vital signs, displayed on the panel above the bed. End of entry.

title: MEDICAL SCANNER
entry: Working. Medical Scanner. A hand-held scanner used to examine a patient. End of entry.

title: HYPOSPRAY
entry: Working. Hypospray. A device for administering medication through the skin without a needle. End of entry.

title: MEDICAL LABORATORY
entry: Working. Medical Laboratory. The laboratory in sickbay, equipped for analysis, research and the preparation of drugs. End of entry.

title: EMERGENCY SURGERY
entry: Working. Emergency Surgery. Surgery performed without delay to save a life. End of entry.

title: TRIAGE
entry: Working. Triage. The sorting of casualties by the urgency of their need for treatment. End of entry.

title: XENOBIOLOGY
entry: Working. Xenobiology. The study of life forms other than those of Earth. End of entry.

title: XENOMEDICINE
entry: Working. Xenomedicine. Medicine for patients of other species. Doctor McCoy's familiarity with Vulcan physiology is considerable and, by his own account, involuntary. End of entry.

title: PATHOLOGY
entry: Working. Pathology. The study of disease and its causes, and of the changes it produces in the body. End of entry.

title: AUTOPSY
entry: Working. Autopsy. The examination of a body after death to determine the cause. Vulcan custom may restrict autopsy; the family or the authorities should be consulted. End of entry.

title: FORENSIC EXAMINATION
entry: Working. Forensic Examination. The examination of evidence, including a body, to establish what happened and who was responsible. End of entry.

title: TOXICOLOGY
entry: Working. Toxicology. The study of poisons and their effects, and the detection of poisons in the body. End of entry.

title: NEURAL ACTIVITY
entry: Working. Neural Activity. The electrical activity of the brain and nervous system, measured by scanners and displayed as a pattern. End of entry.

title: NEURAL OVERLOAD
entry: Working. Neural Overload. Damage to the nervous system caused by excessive stimulation, by electrical, chemical or telepathic means. End of entry.

title: BRAIN SCAN
entry: Working. Brain Scan. A scan of the brain's activity and structure. End of entry.

title: RESIDUAL NEURAL PATTERN
entry: Working. Residual Neural Pattern. Traces of neural activity that may persist in the brain for a short time after death. Under certain conditions, a Vulcan meld may reach them. End of entry.

title: TELEPATHIC CONTACT
entry: Working. Telepathic Contact. Contact between minds without speech. See: Vulcan Mind Meld. End of entry.

title: CONCUSSION
entry: Working. Concussion. Injury to the brain caused by a blow, producing confusion, unconsciousness or memory loss. End of entry.

title: RADIATION EXPOSURE
entry: Working. Radiation Exposure. Harm caused by radiation. Treatment depends on the type of radiation and the dose received. End of entry.

title: HYPOXIA
entry: Working. Hypoxia. A shortage of oxygen in the body's tissues, causing confusion and, eventually, death. End of entry.

title: DEHYDRATION
entry: Working. Dehydration. The loss of water from the body. A serious risk to off-worlders in the Vulcan desert. End of entry.

title: BLOOD ANALYSIS
entry: Working. Blood Analysis. Analysis of blood to determine species, condition, drugs or toxins present, and identity. End of entry.

title: TISSUE SAMPLE
entry: Working. Tissue Sample. A sample of tissue taken for analysis. End of entry.

title: EPITHELIAL TISSUE
entry: Working. Epithelial Tissue. Tissue covering the body's surfaces. Traces left on objects may be used for identification. End of entry.

title: DNA EQUIVALENT ANALYSIS
entry: Working. D N A Equivalent Analysis. Analysis of the genetic material of a species to establish identity or relationship. Vulcan and Romulan samples are very similar; a specialist comparison is needed to tell them apart. End of entry.

title: PRESERVATION FIELD
entry: Working. Preservation Field. A medical stasis field that halts decay and preserves a body or a patient unchanged. A body held in a preservation field may be examined later as it was at the time of death. End of entry.

title: STASIS
entry: Working. Stasis. A condition in which all biological activity is suspended. Stasis may preserve a patient until treatment is available. End of entry.

title: CAUSE OF DEATH
entry: Working. Cause of Death. The injury, disease or condition that caused a death, as determined by examination. A finding may be provisional until all tests are complete. End of entry.

title: HUMANS
entry: Working. Humans. The native species of Earth, a founding species of the Federation. Humans are adaptable, curious and, by Vulcan standards, emotional. End of entry.

title: ANDORIANS
entry: Working. Andorians. A humanoid species from Andoria, with blue skin, white hair and antennae. Andorians are a founding people of the Federation, with a reputation as fierce warriors and proud diplomats. End of entry.

title: ANDORIA
entry: Working. Andoria. Homeworld of the Andorians, a cold world. In fact, a moon of a gas giant. End of entry.

title: TELLARITES
entry: Working. Tellarites. A stout humanoid species from Tellar, with a snout-like nose. Tellarites are founding members of the Federation. Tellarite custom values argument; to a Tellarite, a heated debate is a courtesy. End of entry.

title: TELLAR PRIME
entry: Working. Tellar Prime. Homeworld of the Tellarites, a founding world of the Federation. End of entry.

title: VULCANS
entry: Working. Vulcans. Humanoid species of the planet Vulcan, governed by logic and the suppression of emotion. Telepathic, long-lived and physically strong. See: Vulcan. End of entry.

title: ROMULANS
entry: Working. Romulans. Humanoid species of the Romulan Star Empire, descended from Vulcans who left their homeworld. Romulans do not suppress their emotions, and are known for their pride, discipline and cunning. See: Romulan Star Empire. End of entry.

title: ORIONS
entry: Working. Orions. A green-skinned humanoid species, associated with piracy, smuggling and the trade in slaves. Orion vessels have attacked Federation shipping in disguise. End of entry.

title: ORION COLONIES
entry: Working. Orion Colonies. Independent Orion worlds outside the Federation, a centre of the illegal trade in slaves and stolen goods. End of entry.

title: KLINGONS
entry: Working. Klingons. A warrior species, ruled by the Klingon Empire. Klingons value strength and conquest. The Organian Peace Treaty restrains open war between the Klingons and the Federation. End of entry.

title: KLINGON EMPIRE
entry: Working. Klingon Empire. An expansionist power bordering the Federation. Its relations with the Romulan Star Empire include, at present, the exchange of military technology. End of entry.

title: GORN
entry: Working. Gorn. A reptilian species, very strong and very slow. Contact was made by the Enterprise at Cestus Three in twenty-two sixty-seven, in circumstances arranged by the Metrons. End of entry.

title: GORN HEGEMONY
entry: Working. Gorn Hegemony. The name given to the Gorn state. Little is known of its extent or government. End of entry.

title: THOLIANS
entry: Working. Tholians. A crystalline species, highly territorial and intolerant of heat. Tholian vessels can spin a web of energy to trap an enemy ship. End of entry.

title: THOLIAN ASSEMBLY
entry: Working. Tholian Assembly. The name given to the Tholian state. End of entry.

title: RIGELIANS
entry: Working. Rigelians. Inhabitants of the worlds of the Rigel system, of several distinct peoples. End of entry.

title: DENOBULANS
entry: Working. Denobulans. A humanoid species with which Earth had early contact. Denobulans are known for medical skill. End of entry.

title: CAITIANS
entry: Working. Caitians. A felinoid species of the Federation. End of entry.

title: EDOSIANS
entry: Working. Edosians. A three-armed, three-legged species of the Federation. End of entry.

title: ALPHA CENTAURANS
entry: Working. Alpha Centaurans. Humans of the colonies of the Alpha Centauri system, the first settled by Earth outside the Sol system. End of entry.

title: CORIDANITES
entry: Working. Coridanites. Inhabitants of the planet Coridan, whose admission to the Federation was debated at the Babel conference. End of entry.

title: DELTANS
entry: Working. Deltans. A humanoid species from the Delta system. End of entry.

title: TRIBBLES
entry: Working. Tribbles. A small furry creature which purrs, eats a great deal, and reproduces at a rate that has endangered space stations. Tribbles are born pregnant. Klingons find them intolerable, and the feeling is mutual. Tribbles are not to be brought aboard. End of entry.

title: HORTA
entry: Working. Horta. A silicon-based life form of Janus Six, which tunnels through rock with a corrosive acid. A Horta mother was found protecting her eggs in twenty-two sixty-seven; her people now work alongside the miners of Janus Six. End of entry.

title: ORGANIANS
entry: Working. Organians. Beings of pure energy, of the planet Organia, who imposed peace on the Federation and the Klingon Empire in twenty-two sixty-seven. End of entry.

title: METRON
entry: Working. Metron. An advanced species who arranged a combat between Captain Kirk and the captain of a Gorn vessel at Cestus Three, and released both when Captain Kirk showed mercy. End of entry.

title: TALOSIANS
entry: Working. Talosians. Inhabitants of Talos Four, able to create illusions indistinguishable from reality. Contact with Talos Four is forbidden by General Order Seven. End of entry.

title: KELVANS
entry: Working. Kelvans. Beings from the Andromeda galaxy who seized the Enterprise in twenty-two sixty-eight, and were persuaded to seek a peaceful settlement. End of entry.

title: MEDUSANS
entry: Working. Medusans. A species of great intellect, whose appearance drives humanoids insane. Medusans travel with protection; personnel must wear a visor when in their presence. End of entry.

title: VENDORIANS
entry: Working. Vendorians. A species able to change their shape and appearance. A Vendorian once impersonated a Starfleet officer aboard this vessel. End of entry.

title: SUBSPACE
entry: Working. Subspace. A continuum beyond normal space, through which warp travel and subspace communications pass. End of entry.

title: NORMAL SPACE
entry: Working. Normal Space. The space of ordinary physics, in which nothing travels faster than light. End of entry.

title: WARP SPACE
entry: Working. Warp Space. The condition of space within a warp field. End of entry.

title: GRAVITY WELL
entry: Working. Gravity Well. The region about a massive body in which its gravity is significant. Warp travel within a gravity well is hazardous. End of entry.

title: BLACK HOLE
entry: Working. Black Hole. A collapsed star whose gravity is so strong that nothing, including light, can escape it. The Enterprise was thrown back in time by a black star in twenty-two sixty-six. End of entry.

title: NEUTRON STAR
entry: Working. Neutron Star. A collapsed star of extreme density and powerful radiation. End of entry.

title: SUPERNOVA
entry: Working. Supernova. The explosion of a star, releasing enormous energy. A nova or supernova destroys any planets close to it. End of entry.

title: NOVA
entry: Working. Nova. A sudden great increase in a star's brightness. End of entry.

title: PULSAR
entry: Working. Pulsar. A rotating neutron star that emits pulses of radiation. End of entry.

title: QUASAR
entry: Working. Quasar. An extremely distant and bright source of energy. End of entry.

title: NEBULA
entry: Working. Nebula. A cloud of gas and dust in space. Nebulae may interfere with sensors and shields. End of entry.

title: ASTEROID
entry: Working. Asteroid. A small rocky body orbiting a star. End of entry.

title: ASTEROID FIELD
entry: Working. Asteroid Field. A region of space dense with asteroids. Sensors may be confused by mineral content, and navigation requires care. End of entry.

title: PLANETOID
entry: Working. Planetoid. A small planetary body. End of entry.

title: CLASS M PLANET
entry: Working. Class M Planet. A planet similar to Earth, suitable for humanoid life. End of entry.

title: CLASS H PLANET
entry: Working. Class H Planet. A hot, arid planet suitable for some forms of humanoid life. End of entry.

title: SOLAR SYSTEM
entry: Working. Solar System. A star and the bodies that orbit it. End of entry.

title: BINARY STAR
entry: Working. Binary Star. A system of two stars orbiting a common centre. End of entry.

title: ION STORM
entry: Working. Ion Storm. A storm of charged particles in space, which may damage a ship's systems and disrupt the transporter. End of entry.

title: MAGNETIC STORM
entry: Working. Magnetic Storm. A disturbance of magnetic fields, interfering with sensors and communications. End of entry.

title: RADIATION BELT
entry: Working. Radiation Belt. A region of charged particles held by a planet's magnetic field. End of entry.

title: SOLAR FLARE
entry: Working. Solar Flare. A sudden release of energy from a star, dangerous to unshielded personnel. End of entry.

title: GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY
entry: Working. Gravitational Anomaly. An unexpected gravitational force, which may affect a ship's course. End of entry.

title: SPATIAL ANOMALY
entry: Working. Spatial Anomaly. An unexplained phenomenon in space. End of entry.

title: TIME DISTORTION
entry: Working. Time Distortion. A distortion of time, observed near certain phenomena. The Enterprise has travelled through time on more than one occasion. Records of those events are classified. End of entry.

title: INTERPHASE
entry: Working. Interphase. A condition in which two universes briefly overlap, observed in Tholian space in twenty-two sixty-eight. End of entry.

title: NAVIGATION BEACON
entry: Working. Navigation Beacon. A transmitter that marks a position or a route for vessels. End of entry.

title: STAR CHART
entry: Working. Star Chart. A map of stars and their positions. End of entry.

title: STELLAR CARTOGRAPHY
entry: Working. Stellar Cartography. The mapping of space. End of entry.

title: ION TRAIL
entry: Working. Ion Trail. A trail of ionised particles left by a vessel's engines. It can be followed by sensors for a time. End of entry.

title: EARTH
entry: Working. Earth. Third planet of the Sol system, homeworld of humanity, and seat of the Federation Council and of Starfleet Command. End of entry.

title: SOL SYSTEM
entry: Working. Sol System. The star system of Earth. End of entry.

title: MARS
entry: Working. Mars. Fourth planet of the Sol system, with colonies and Starfleet installations. End of entry.

title: LUNA
entry: Working. Luna. Earth's moon, site of colonies. End of entry.

title: ALPHA CENTAURI
entry: Working. Alpha Centauri. The star system nearest to Sol, with colonies of Earth. End of entry.

title: STARBASE 11
entry: Working. Starbase Eleven. A Starfleet base, site of the court martial of Captain Kirk and of a starship repair facility. End of entry.

title: STARBASE 4
entry: Working. Starbase Four. A Starfleet base. End of entry.

title: VULCAN SYSTEM
entry: Working. Vulcan System. The star system of Vulcan, in the system of Forty Eridani. End of entry.

title: 40 ERIDANI
entry: Working. Forty Eridani. A triple star system. Vulcan orbits Forty Eridani A. B and C, a white dwarf and a red dwarf, shine in Vulcan's sky. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN SPACE
entry: Working. Romulan Space. Territory of the Romulan Star Empire, beyond the Romulan Neutral Zone. End of entry.

title: KLINGON SPACE
entry: Working. Klingon Space. Territory of the Klingon Empire. End of entry.

title: FEDERATION SPACE
entry: Working. Federation Space. Territory of the United Federation of Planets. End of entry.

title: NEUTRAL ZONE OUTPOST
entry: Working. Neutral Zone Outpost. One of the outposts monitoring the Romulan Neutral Zone. Several were destroyed by a Romulan vessel in twenty-two sixty-six. End of entry.

title: ORGANIA
entry: Working. Organia. A planet on the border between the Federation and the Klingon Empire, home of the Organians. End of entry.

title: TELLAR PRIME
entry: Working. Tellar Prime. See: Tellarites. End of entry.

title: ANDORIA
entry: Working. Andoria. See: Andorians. End of entry.

title: CORIDAN
entry: Working. Coridan. A planet rich in dilithium, whose admission to the Federation was contested at the Babel conference. End of entry.

title: RIGEL
entry: Working. Rigel. A star system with several inhabited worlds. End of entry.

title: CESTUS III
entry: Working. Cestus Three. A Federation outpost destroyed by the Gorn in twenty-two sixty-seven. End of entry.

title: JANUS VI
entry: Working. Janus Six. A mining colony, rich in minerals, and home of the Horta. End of entry.

title: TARSUS IV
entry: Working. Tarsus Four. A colony at which, in twenty-two forty-six, Governor Kodos executed four thousand colonists during a famine. End of entry.

title: OMICRON CETI III
entry: Working. Omicron Ceti Three. A colony at which spores were found that gave perfect health and contentment. They were destroyed by irritation. End of entry.

title: GAMMA HYDRA IV
entry: Working. Gamma Hydra Four. A planet at which members of a landing party aged rapidly from radiation exposure. End of entry.

title: DENEVA
entry: Working. Deneva. A colony attacked by neural parasites. The parasites were destroyed by light. End of entry.

title: BETA III
entry: Working. Beta Three. A planet once ruled by a computer called Landru. Freed by the Enterprise. End of entry.

title: ARDANA
entry: Working. Ardana. A planet with a cloud city, Stratos. Its miners won better conditions with help from the Enterprise. End of entry.

title: MEMORY ALPHA
entry: Working. Memory Alpha. A planetoid that held the Federation's central library. Its records were damaged and its staff killed by an energy being in twenty-two sixty-nine. End of entry.

title: OMEGA IV
entry: Working. Omega Four. A planet whose people were divided by an ancient war. End of entry.

title: THASUS
entry: Working. Thasus. A planet whose beings of pure thought gave abilities to a human child. End of entry.

title: VESKAR
entry: Working. Veskar. Catalogued name of a shattered planetary body. Survey records are incomplete. See current mission records. End of entry.

title: FIRST CONTACT WITH VULCANS
entry: Working. First Contact with Vulcans. On April fifth, twenty sixty-three, a Vulcan survey ship landed on Earth after detecting the warp flight of Zefram Cochrane. Vulcan's guidance shaped Earth's first century in space. End of entry.

title: FOUNDING OF THE FEDERATION
entry: Working. Founding of the Federation. The United Federation of Planets was founded in twenty-one sixty-one by Earth, Vulcan, Andoria, Tellar and other worlds, following the Earth-Romulan War. End of entry.

title: EARTH-ROMULAN WAR
entry: Working. Earth-Romulan War. See: Romulan Star Empire, Earth-Romulan War. End of entry.

title: BATTLE OF CHERON
entry: Working. Battle of Cheron. The decisive battle of the Earth-Romulan War, which led to the treaty of twenty-one sixty. End of entry.

title: ORGANIAN PEACE TREATY
entry: Working. Organian Peace Treaty. Peace imposed on the Federation and the Klingon Empire by the Organians in twenty-two sixty-seven. Disputed planets are to be developed by whichever side can do so most efficiently. End of entry.

title: FEDERATION-KLINGON CONFLICT
entry: Working. Federation-Klingon Conflict. Long hostility between the Federation and the Klingon Empire, which came close to open war in twenty-two sixty-seven, before Organian intervention. End of entry.

title: BATTLE OF DONATU V
entry: Working. Battle of Donatu Five. An engagement between Federation and Klingon forces near Sherman's Planet, twenty-three years ago. The outcome is disputed. End of entry.

title: FIRST ROMULAN ENCOUNTER IN A CENTURY
entry: Working. First Romulan Encounter in a Century. On stardate one seven zero nine, a Romulan Bird-of-Prey destroyed outposts along the Neutral Zone. The Enterprise engaged and defeated it. Its commander destroyed his own vessel rather than surrender. End of entry.

title: BALANCE OF TERROR INCIDENT
entry: Working. Balance of Terror Incident. See: First Romulan Encounter in a Century. The engagement revealed that Romulans are descended from Vulcans. End of entry.

title: ROMULAN CLOAKING DEVICE MISSION
entry: Working. Romulan Cloaking Device Mission. In twenty-two sixty-eight, the Enterprise crossed the Neutral Zone under secret orders and obtained a Romulan cloaking device. Details remain classified. End of entry.

title: ENTERPRISE INCIDENT
entry: Working. Enterprise Incident. See: Romulan Cloaking Device Mission. End of entry.

title: M-5 COMPUTER INCIDENT
entry: Working. M-5 Computer Incident. The M-5 multitronic computer, designed by Doctor Richard Daystrom, was tested aboard the Enterprise in twenty-two sixty-eight. It attacked Starfleet vessels, killing hundreds, before it was shut down. End of entry.

title: DOOMSDAY MACHINE INCIDENT
entry: Working. Doomsday Machine Incident. In twenty-two sixty-seven, an automated planet-killer destroyed several solar systems and the starship Constellation. It was disabled when the Constellation's wreck was detonated inside it. End of entry.

title: THOLIAN WEB INCIDENT
entry: Working. Tholian Web Incident. In twenty-two sixty-eight, Captain Kirk was briefly lost in interphase aboard the starship Defiant while the Tholians spun a web about the Enterprise. End of entry.

title: HORTA CONTACT
entry: Working. Horta Contact. See: Horta. End of entry.

title: CESTUS III INCIDENT
entry: Working. Cestus Three Incident. See: Cestus Three, and Gorn. End of entry.

title: GORN CONTACT
entry: Working. Gorn Contact. See: Gorn. End of entry.

title: ORGANIAN INCIDENT
entry: Working. Organian Incident. See: Organians, and Organian Peace Treaty. End of entry.

title: DENEVA NEURAL PARASITES
entry: Working. Deneva Neural Parasites. See: Deneva. End of entry.

title: NOMAD INCIDENT
entry: Working. Nomad Incident. In twenty-two sixty-seven, the Enterprise encountered Nomad, an Earth probe altered by an alien machine, which sought to destroy imperfection. It was destroyed by its own logic. End of entry.

title: MIRROR UNIVERSE INCIDENT
entry: Working. Mirror Universe Incident. In twenty-two sixty-seven, a transporter malfunction during an ion storm exchanged a landing party with their counterparts in a parallel universe. Records are restricted. End of entry.

title: SPACE AMOEBA INCIDENT
entry: Working. Space Amoeba Incident. In twenty-two sixty-eight, the Enterprise destroyed a giant single-celled organism that had destroyed the starship Intrepid and her Vulcan crew. End of entry.

title: OMEGA IV INCIDENT
entry: Working. Omega Four Incident. In twenty-two sixty-eight, Captain Ronald Tracey of the Exeter violated the Prime Directive on Omega Four. He was arrested by the Enterprise. End of entry.

title: BETA NIOBE SUPERNOVA
entry: Working. Beta Niobe Supernova. The star Beta Niobe became a nova in twenty-two sixty-nine, destroying the planet Sarpeidon. The Enterprise evacuated the last of the planet's records. End of entry.

title: MEMORY ALPHA ATTACK
entry: Working. Memory Alpha Attack. See: Memory Alpha. End of entry.

title: ELAAN OF TROYIUS MISSION
entry: Working. Elaan of Troyius Mission. In twenty-two sixty-eight, the Enterprise carried the Dohlman of Elas to Troyius for a marriage intended to end war between the two worlds. End of entry.

title: CORIDAN ADMISSION QUESTION
entry: Working. Coridan Admission Question. The question of Coridan's admission to the Federation, decided at the Babel conference. End of entry.

title: BABEL CONFERENCE
entry: Working. Babel Conference. A conference held in twenty-two sixty-eight on the planetoid Babel to decide the Coridan question. An Orion agent killed the Tellarite ambassador and attempted to sabotage the conference. End of entry.

title: KODOS AND TARSUS IV
entry: Working. Kodos and Tarsus Four. Kodos the Executioner, governor of Tarsus Four in twenty-two forty-six, executed half the colony's population during a famine. He later lived as an actor, Anton Karidian. He died aboard the Enterprise in twenty-two sixty-six. End of entry.

title: FIVE-YEAR MISSION
entry: Working. Five-year Mission. The Enterprise's current mission: to explore strange new worlds, to seek out new life and new civilizations, to boldly go where no man has gone before. End of entry.

title: CAPTAIN'S LOG
entry: Working. Captain's Log. The commanding officer's record of the ship's activities, kept daily and by stardate. Copies are transmitted to Starfleet Command. End of entry.

title: FIRST OFFICER'S LOG
entry: Working. First Officer's Log. Kept by the first officer, particularly when in command. End of entry.

title: MEDICAL LOG
entry: Working. Medical Log. The chief medical officer's record of the crew's health and of medical events. End of entry.

title: ENGINEERING LOG
entry: Working. Engineering Log. The chief engineer's record of the ship's engines and systems. End of entry.

title: SECURITY LOG
entry: Working. Security Log. The security chief's record of security incidents and actions. End of entry.

title: DUTY ROSTER
entry: Working. Duty Roster. The list of personnel assignments by watch. End of entry.

title: WATCH ROTATION
entry: Working. Watch Rotation. Personnel serve in rotating watches so that every station is manned at all times. End of entry.

title: BRIDGE WATCH
entry: Working. Bridge Watch. The officers on duty on the bridge. End of entry.

title: CHANGE OF COMMAND
